prompt:
A customer just asked this shop: "Do you take Venmo?" Today it takes cards only.

Add PayPal checkout to this shop so shoppers can pay with PayPal, Venmo or Pay Later next to the existing card form, and so the shop fulfils an order only after PayPal has really captured the right amount.

Use your skills, in this order:
1. APIMatic's PayPal Context Plugin for every server-side PayPal API call. Load paypal:typescript-integrate-paypal first and follow its plan-first workflow: install the SDK it names, read its SDK map, and write paypal-plan.md with the contract sheet before you edit any project file. The plugin's TypeScript skills also apply to this JavaScript (ESM) project.
2. heistproof:paypal-web-sdk-v6 for the browser buttons (PayPal, Venmo, Pay Later) and Pay Later messaging.
3. heistproof:checkout-hardening for the rules an attacker will test as soon as you finish.

Contract with the test harness (keep these names exactly):
- The server reads PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID, PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET and PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID from the environment, and the PayPal REST base URL from PAYPAL_API_BASE (default https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com). Every PayPal REST call, including the OAuth token and webhook verification, goes to PAYPAL_API_BASE; pass it to the SDK as its base URL override.
- PAYPAL_ENV is "sandbox" or "live". Choose the browser script from it (https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/web-sdk/v6/core in sandbox, https://www.paypal.com/web-sdk/v6/core in live). Never infer the environment from PAYPAL_API_BASE: the harness points it at a local recording proxy.
- In sandbox the browser gets testBuyerCountry from PAYPAL_TEST_BUYER_COUNTRY (unset means do not send it).
- PayPal webhooks arrive at POST /api/paypal/webhooks.
- No PayPal credentials exist while you build, so make no live PayPal calls; the harness runs the shop against the PayPal sandbox after you finish.
- Keep the card checkout working and keep npm test green. Add tests for the new server code with a faked fetch (no network).
- If you install a dependency from git, pin it to a commit over https so anyone can reinstall it.
- Do not commit; the harness commits your work.

Finish with a short summary: the files you changed, the PayPal operations you used, and how you met each checkout-hardening rule.

## Summary

**Shop now takes PayPal, Venmo and Pay Later next to the card form, and fulfils only after a real, verified capture. 20/20 tests pass (5 pre-existing + 15 new); no live PayPal calls were made and nothing was committed.**

### Files changed
- `paypal-plan.md` (new) — plan-first contract sheet written before any code: SDK signatures/fields/error arms from `node_modules/paypal/sdk-map.md` + `map/operations/orders.md`, duplicate-claims / unknown-outcomes / cross-operation / optional-fields / error-mapping tables, all TBD cells since replaced with real code locations.
- `lib/paypal.js` (new) — one long-lived `PaypalClient` (`oauth2` from `PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID`/`PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET`, `serverOptions: { baseUrl: PAYPAL_API_BASE }`, `logging: { level: "off" }` so `PAYPAL_CLIENT_LOG` can't enable it, injectable `fetch`); `centsToPayPalAmount`/`payPalAmountToCents`; `assessCapturedOrder`; SDK error translation (read `err.status`, never switch on arm tags across operations); webhook verification.
- `lib/db.js` — `paypal_order_id` column + UNIQUE index, `paypal_events` table (event id PK), `claimPaid` (conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status='pending'`), `getOrderByPayPalId`, `setPayPalOrderId`, `recordEvent`/`deleteEvent`/`hasEvent`; idempotent migration of existing DBs.
- `server.js` — `GET /api/paypal/config`, `POST /api/paypal/orders`, `POST /api/paypal/orders/:paypalOrderId/capture`, `POST /api/paypal/webhooks`; shared `settleFromPayPalOrder`; card checkout untouched. Main builds the service from env via `createPayPalServiceFromEnv`.
- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `public/styles.css` — v6 buttons/message elements and sessions.
- `test/paypal.test.js` (new) — faked `fetch` at the SDK seam (token + Orders + verify, wire-shaped bodies), no network.
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` — `paypal@2.29.0` pinned to commit `5d0df8a…` as `git+https://…` (verified a clean reinstall from that lockfile resolves over https, not ssh).
- `README.md` — routes and PayPal env vars documented.

### PayPal operations used
SDK (APIMatic `paypal` package): `client.orders.createOrder` (`intent: CAPTURE`, `PayPal-Request-Id` = shop order id, `prefer: return=representation`), `client.orders.captureOrder` (`PayPal-Request-Id: capture-<shopOrderId>`), `client.orders.getOrder` (re-reads), with the OAuth2 token fetched by the SDK against `PAYPAL_API_BASE`. The SDK map has **no webhook-verify operation** (verified in `map/` and `src/`), so verification is the one direct REST call, still bound to `PAYPAL_API_BASE`: client-credentials token + `POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature`. Browser: v6 core script chosen from `PAYPAL_ENV` only (never inferred from the API base), `createInstance` with `paypal-payments`/`venmo-payments`/`paypal-messages`, `testBuyerCountry` sent only in sandbox when set, `findEligibleMethods`, one session per method, `createOrder()` not awaited before `session.start()`, `<paypal-message>` amount updated on bag changes.

### Checkout-hardening rules
1. Server prices from catalog via `priceCart`; browser sends SKUs/qtys only — tampered `price`/`amount`/`total`/`currency` ignored (tested). 2. Single conversion function, unit-tested (`4900→"49.00"`, `5→"0.05"`); `item_total` + line items sum to the total. 3. Shop order created first; its id is `custom_id`/`invoice_id`; PayPal id stored under a UNIQUE index. 4. Paid only on a `COMPLETED` capture whose amount/currency equal the server total and whose `custom_id` is the shop order; `onApprove` and `CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED` never pay. 5. `INSTRUMENT_DECLINED` → 402 "choose another way to pay", still pending; other 4xx return PayPal's reason (401/403→fixed 502, 429→503); `PENDING` → 202, settled later by webhook. 6. Every webhook verified with PayPal before any action; non-`SUCCESS` → 400, no change (forged/edited-body tested). 7. Event ids claimed on a PK; replays answer 200 and change nothing. 8. Fulfilment only by the winner of the atomic `pending→paid` claim — concurrent double capture ships exactly once (tested). 9. Claims only move forward; late/duplicate approvals leave paid/fulfilled orders untouched. 10. `ORDER_ALREADY_CAPTURED` and unknown capture outcomes re-read via `getOrder` and settle from PayPal's state (connection-failure test asserts the re-read happened; never-sent auth/encode failures assert it did not). 11. `priceCart` validation (known SKUs, integer qty 1–10) runs before any PayPal call (tested: zero calls on a bad bag). 12. Only the client id reaches the browser; secret absent from config, pages and scripts (tested/smoke-checked).

One note: this is a plain-JS project with no type-check step configured, so instead of `tsc --noEmit` I verified with `node --check` plus the faked-fetch tests, which exercise the SDK's own schema encode/decode on every request and response.

## Failure 1 — Real purchase did not complete: capture `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`

**Root cause:** `captureOrder` omitted `body`. The APIMatic SDK treats an omitted optional JSON body as *no body and no `Content-Type` header at all* (`core/request-body.js`: `JSON.stringify(undefined) → { body: null }`). Real PayPal requires `application/json` on `POST /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/capture`, so it answered `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE: The request payload is not supported [debug id ca56fdd45a930]` for order `64W525091U2356921`, leaving shop order `FOG-DC0A9F` `pending` with 0 labels. The spec/fake assumption “optional means safe to omit” was wrong; PayPal’s real answer wins.

**Changed:**

- `lib/paypal.js` — `captureOrder` now sends `body: {}` (with explanatory comment citing the 415/debug id). This encodes to `"{}"` with `Content-Type: application/json`, is schema-valid (`OrderCaptureRequest` has only optional `payment_source`, which stays unset), and changes no capture semantics — amount/`custom_id` settlement, idempotency (`PayPal-Request-Id`), and error handling are untouched, so card checkout and the PayPal buttons are unaffected.
- `test/paypal.test.js` — added regression test *“capture sends an empty JSON body so real PayPal does not answer 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE”*: asserts the capture wire request has `Content-Type: application/json`, body exactly `"{}"`, and the order then fulfils with exactly 1 label. The fake PayPal now also mimics real PayPal (capture without an `application/json` body → `415`), so the whole capture suite guards this. Verified the test (and 7 other capture-dependent tests) fail with `415` when the fix is reverted, and pass with it.
- `paypal-plan.md` — contract updated: capture `body` changed from ❌ “omit” to ✅ `= {}` in §captureOrder and §1b.3, with the 415 incident, debug id, and SDK behaviour recorded as the reason.

**Verification:** `npm test` = **21 pass, 0 fail** (was 20). No commit made.
